Subjective: Oreo, a 3-year-old Labrador recently adopted, was bitten by a street dog about one hour ago. The owner noticed bruising near the thigh with no active bleeding but visible marks. Oreo has not received any vaccinations, deworming, or tick and flea control since adoption.
Objective: Physical examination revealed a small wound near the thigh with bruising. No active bleeding observed. Multiple ticks present on the body. No prior vaccination or parasite control noted.
Assessment: Dog bite wound with risk of rabies exposure due to lack of prior vaccination in both Oreo and the biting street dog. Risk of secondary bacterial infection at wound site. Presence of ticks and lack of deworming increases risk of parasitic burden which may affect vaccine efficacy.
Plan: Administer post-exposure antirabies vaccine following the 5-dose schedule (days 0, 3, 7, 14, 28). Initiate wound dressing and start a 5-day course of systemic antibiotics. Prescribe topical antibiotic ointment for wound care. Administer deworming tablet and Bravecto tablet for tick and flea control today. Provide pain medication to manage wound discomfort. Advise strict indoor confinement to prevent further exposure. Schedule follow-up consultation in one week to assess wound healing and monitor clinical status. After completion of antirabies vaccination, start core MCV vaccine after a two-week gap to protect against other infectious diseases.
Conclusion: Oreo is at risk of rabies and secondary infection due to dog bite and lack of prior vaccination. Immediate post-exposure prophylaxis and supportive care are essential. Parasite control and vaccination schedule adherence are critical for full recovery and prevention of future infections.
DifferentialDiagnosis: Rabies infection (post-exposure), secondary bacterial wound infection, tick-borne diseases, parasitic infestation due to lack of deworming.
KeyIssues: Dog bite wound, risk of rabies exposure, lack of prior vaccination, presence of ticks, no deworming, need for post-exposure prophylaxis and parasite control.
AbnormalFindings: Small wound with bruising near thigh, multiple ticks on body, no prior vaccination or parasite control.
CustomerInstructions: Keep Oreo indoors and restrict outdoor access during treatment and observation period. Administer all prescribed medications including antibiotics, pain medication, deworming, and tick/flea control tablets as directed. Follow the antirabies vaccine schedule strictly. Monitor Oreo for any signs of illness or unusual behavior for at least six months. Book follow-up consultation in one week for wound assessment. Contact the clinic immediately if symptoms worsen or new symptoms appear.
Protocols: Post-exposure antirabies vaccination protocol with five doses on days 0, 3, 7, 14, and 28. Wound care with dressing and topical antibiotics. Systemic antibiotic therapy for 5 days. Deworming and tick/flea control with Bravecto tablet. Pain management as needed. Follow-up consultation after 5 days of antibiotics. Core MCV vaccination to be started two weeks after completion of antirabies vaccination.
Reminders: Observe Oreo for clinical symptoms for six months post-exposure. Adhere to vaccination and medication schedules. Schedule follow-up consultation in one week. Maintain indoor confinement to reduce risk of further exposure.
